title: Washington County Library unveils new community-designed library cards
text:
Washington County Library unveils new community-designed library cards
I. F. Cooper
New community-designed library cards are now available at all Washington County Library branches, the library announced on Sept. 2.
Earlier this year, more than 200 designs were submitted by community members as part of the first Community Library Card Design Contest. Library staff selected finalists in three age groups—kids, teens, and adults—and the public voted for their favorites in June. Nearly 1,550 votes were cast in total.
The winning designs were created by Laila Rick from Valley Library (Lakeland) for kids, Caitlynn Pantenburg from R.H. Stafford Library (Woodbury) for teens, and Darcy Veum from Park Grove Library (Cottage Grove) for adults. New cardholders can now choose from nine different library card designs. Current cardholders also have the option to swap their existing cards for one of the new designs if they wish.
The Washington County Board of Commissioners recognized the contest winners this week. Photographs provided show Laila Rick with Commissioner Bethany Cox and Library Director Jacquie Kramer at Valley Library; Caitlynn Pantenburg with the Board of Commissioners; and Darcy Veum with the Board as well.
More information about obtaining a new or replacement library card is available on the Washington County website.
